title: Avro buffered encoding preserves the caller’s byte window
summary: Writing a bounded window twice must emit the same bytes twice and leave the caller’s cursor usable across the bulk-write threshold.

change.description: The parent hands the caller’s view to the output channel on a bulk write. The fix passes a separate read-only view, preserving the caller’s position.

verdictLabel: Finite JVM 4/4, both native observations on 14/16 inputs per revision
notes: The mapped-buffer upstream test failed on the parent and passed on the fix. Four finite JVM claims cover every selector. The parent advanced the caller’s read-only buffer at selectors 11 and 15, causing the repeated write to omit its second 17-byte copy. The native buffered path covers the other fourteen inputs on each revision. The channel path reaches the JDK's interrupt registration. A pre-interrupted JVM throws ClosedByInterruptException after consuming the channel view. Eight selectors fit the earlier six-byte proof, and a requalified twenty-byte heap-window proof covers the entire grid. See verification/domain-foundations/expansion.json.

Sixteen inputs cross writable and read-only heap views, starting positions zero and two, and lengths zero, four, sixteen and seventeen. The encoder uses its public minimum buffer size of 32. The upstream regression uses a mapped buffer of length seventeen.
